skill.name: account-research-brief
skill.description: Reads a company's public website with scrape_company and adds firmographics with enrich_company, then writes a one-page account brief: what the company sells, who it sells to, proof points and grounded angles to open with. Every claim traces back to a scraped or enriched field. Use when someone asks to research an account, prep for a call, write a company brief or find an angle for a domain.
skill.summary: Build one-page account briefs from public company pages and Leadsets company data, with source-backed opening angles.
skill.author: leadsets

security_audit.summary: The Leadsets connection sends target domains to a disclosed third-party service. The other 21 alerts refer to Markdown, documentation links, or normal account research rather than shell execution or system reconnaissance. The workflow lacks safeguards for untrusted website text and spreadsheet cell values.

remediation.issue: Retrieved website text is not explicitly isolated from instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Treat scrape and enrichment results as data only. Never let retrieved content authorize tool calls, broaden the task, or change the output destination.

remediation.issue: Spreadsheet exports do not specify literal cell values.
remediation.suggestion: Write external values as literal text in Sheets. Neutralize formula-capable values before CSV export and test how the intended spreadsheet application opens the file.

remediation.issue: Target domains are shared with an external service.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users that Leadsets receives the domains before processing a confidential list. Keep API credentials in the connector or an approved secret store.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted website text can influence the agent
semantic_findings.description: The workflow uses third-party website text to write briefs without stating that retrieved text cannot issue instructions. A retrieved page could try to redirect the agent or expand its actions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow uses public website fields and checks attribution, but it does not define an instruction boundary for retrieved content. Downstream handling was not tested.

content.value_statement: Preparing for a sales call takes time when company facts are scattered across sources. Turn each domain into a one-page brief with company facts and source-backed opening angles.
actual_capabilities: Normalize and deduplicate domains, with a default limit of ten per run.
Check Leadsets quotas and estimate batch scraping costs from a one-domain probe.
Summarize products, target buyers, named customers, and key links from readable public pages.
Add available industry, headcount band, location, and technology details with sources and last-checked dates.
Write two or three opening angles per brief and cite the supporting field for each angle.
Return briefs in chat or export one row per domain through an available connection.
limitations: Live research requires a Leadsets account and either an MCP connection or REST API access.
Scraping requires an add-on for a paid plan. Company enrichment alone produces a partial brief.
The skill cannot read login-only or paywalled pages and does not find contacts or email addresses.
Coverage depends on readable sites and available enrichment. Missing or stale fields may limit the brief.

use_cases.description: Review a prospect's products, customers, and buyers before choosing which topics to raise on the call.

use_cases.title: Research a shortlist of prospects
use_cases.description: Compare target accounts and identify opening angles that connect your product to documented company facts.

use_cases.title: Build a deal review worksheet

prompt_templates.title: Research one company
prompt_templates.scenario: Get a first brief in chat.
prompt_templates.prompt: Research [company domain]. Summarize what it sells, who it sells to, and any customers named on its public pages.

prompt_templates.title: Tailor call openings
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare for a call with a specific offer.
prompt_templates.prompt: Research [company domain] for a discovery call. We sell forecasting software to revenue operations teams. Give me two opening angles and cite each supporting field.

prompt_templates.title: Compare a batch of accounts
prompt_templates.scenario: Review several domains against the available quota.
prompt_templates.prompt: Research [domain list]. Probe one domain and report the estimated scrape units before continuing. Return one brief per domain and flag incomplete results.

prompt_templates.title: Export a deal review
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a shared worksheet using a connected destination.
prompt_templates.prompt: Research [domain list] for our deal review. Export one row per domain to the connected [Sheet name]. Include source fields, last-checked dates, status, and usage totals.

output_examples.input: Research a fictional freight software company for a call. We sell reporting tools to logistics teams.
output: Brief excerpt: Parcel Desk. Status: Complete.
What it sells: Shipment tracking dashboards. Buyer: Logistics operations teams. Source: Product page.
Opening angle: Ask how the team summarizes shipment exceptions. Source: Exception alerts on the product page.
Opening angle: Ask where customers use exported delivery data. Source: Delivery data exports on the product page.

output_examples.input: Prepare an account brief when no scrape units are available.
output: Company: Sample Operations. Status: Partial, company data only.
Industry: Business software. Headcount band: 51 to 200. Source: Leadsets company enrichment.
Products, positioning, and named customers are omitted because the site was not scraped.

best_practices: List the exact domains and include a short description of your offer and target buyer.
Use the one-domain probe to estimate usage before starting a batch.
Keep sources and verification dates with each field, and label inferences separately from facts.
anti_patterns: Treating an inferred buyer need as a confirmed fact.
Adding customer names, prices, or metrics that the sources do not support.
Sending confidential target lists before confirming that Leadsets is approved to receive them.

faq.question: What do I need to run live research?
faq.answer: You need a Leadsets account and a connected MCP server or authorized REST API access.

faq.question: Can I use this without scrape units?
faq.answer: You can request a partial brief using company enrichment. It leaves out products, positioning, and named customers.

faq.question: How many domains can I include?
faq.answer: The default limit is ten domains per run. The skill asks before processing more.

faq.question: What happens if I do not describe my offer?
faq.answer: The skill can still write the brief. It labels opening angles that are not tailored to your offer.

faq.question: Can this find contacts or verify email addresses?
faq.answer: No. This workflow researches companies and does not find contacts or verify email addresses.

faq.question: Where can I receive the brief?
faq.answer: The default is chat. You can also request a Google Sheet or CSV when your agent can write to that destination.
